items.statement: FY27 consolidated volume guidance of 80 million tonnes (8-10% growth)
items.quote: we are expecting it to grow in FY '28 -- '27 by almost, say, 8% to around 80 million-odd tonnes.

items.statement: FY27 cost reduction target of INR250 per tonne (from INR4,500)
items.quote: we are looking at roughly INR250 a tonne reduction this year and then another reduction of INR250 next year as well.

items.statement: Trade sales volume grew to 74% in Q4 FY26 (up from 68% in Q4 FY25)
items.quote: we have also improved our trade sales to 74% compared to in December quarter of '25, it was 68%

items.statement: Premium cement sales accounted for 35-36% of trade sales in Q4 FY26
items.quote: Almost 36% of my trade sales has been premium cement sales for Q4. We will continue to improve the reliability at Penna and Sanghi and th e overall asset

items.statement: Capacity utilization targets for FY27: Sanghi (65-70%), Penna (55-60%), Orient (100%), Ambuja/ACC (75-80%)
items.quote: Orient, for example, is operating at full capacity. So far as Sanghi is concerned, I will peg myself at almost like 65% to 70%. And so far as Penna is concerned, I will consider around 55% to 60%.

items.statement: Capacity expansion to 119 million tonnes by FY27 end (from 109 million tonnes in FY26)
items.quote: We are expecting to hit capacity of almost 119 million tonnes by end of FY '27.

items.statement: FY26 capex was INR7,500 crores; FY27 capex estimated at INR6,000-6,500 crores
items.quote: FY '26 is closer to about INR7,500-odd crores. And I will just answer because there would be another question. So for FY '27, we are keeping an estimate of almost INR6,000 crores to INR6,500 crores.

items.statement: Cost escalation of INR250 per tonne in Q4 FY26 due to geopolitical factors, peaking at INR4,500 per tonne
items.quote: we are sitting at almost INR4,250 for the overall quarter and plus some of these increases what we have seen from the overall escalation. So I would like -- let us say that a normalized was almost INR4,250 and plus another INR250, which we have seen increases. So almost we are at now INR4,500 a tonne for the quarter of

items.statement: Cost reduction expected from fly ash and green energy improvements (INR150-200 per tonne)
items.quote: I strongly believe INR150 to INR200 savings will come from these components.

items.statement: Higher freight costs due to increased sale lead times and state-specific taxes (e.g., Himachal Pradesh)
items.quote: higher freight cost due to increase in the overall sale lead, primary and secondary both, increase in some of the states like the additional goods tax, especially in Himachal.

items.statement: Higher fuel cost due to increased heat consumption and geopolitical factors
items.quote: higher fuel cost on account of a little higher -than-expected heat consumption, what we have and m ore so for the acquired assets, the higher branding cost

items.statement: Packaging cost spikes in March due to West Asia conflict
items.quote: higher packing costs, which we more so have seen that in the month of March, which has seen some abruptions given the West Asia war.

items.statement: Industry demand expected to grow at 5-5.5% in FY27 due to inflation and weak monsoon
items.quote: At an industry level, we believe that given the headlines of inflation and weak monsoon, the industry may grow at around, say, 5% to 5.5%.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 volume growth muted due to packing bag issues and softer demand
items.quote: we also lost a good level of volume because of the packing bag issues and all.

items.statement: Geopolitical tensions and global fuel cost volatility pose risks to cost stability
items.quote: therefore, it will be very difficult to provide any long -term estimates for right now ti ll the time things stabili ze over the next 2, 3

items.statement: Acquired assets (Sanghi, Penna) face operational challenges and lower utilization
items.quote: Sanghi still remains at around, say, at 57% on cement capacity utilization, while Penna is 46%. However, last time I mentioned to you that in December quarter, we have seen a good improvement, especially for Sanghi.

items.statement: Turnaround initiatives for acquired assets delayed, leading to higher maintenance capex
items.quote: some of these plants, especially of Penna, needed higher than expected time for maintenance capex and overall upkeep of the assets.

items.statement: Lower government incentives due to GST rate changes and plant maturity
items.quote: we have also exhausted some of the plants which we are giving -- having the incentives. And third, in some of the states, we are now accruing on incentive on virtual visibility basis.

items.statement: Core working capital days reduced from 30 to 20 days YoY
items.quote: the core working capital, as you also mentioned, has come down and that efficiency of workin g capital will continue

items.statement: Portfolio integration of Sanghi, Penna completed; ACC and Orient Cement amalgamation ongoing
items.quote: Successful amalgamation of Sanghi Industries and Penna Cement with Ambuja Cements is now completed, while ACC and Orient Cement is under process.

items.statement: Focus on organic growth; inorganic opportunities evaluated but not prioritized
items.quote: our primary focus remains organic in terms of stabilizing our ongoing expansions and also already acquired assets. So therefore, I would say that, that remains the primary focus.

items.statement: Management reset: 5 key focus areas (L1 plant discipline, trade sales, raw material/energy cost, channel network, cost reduction)
items.quote: I think the key KPIs that we are putting for ourselves is we need to reduce. We need to -- I would say 5 things that we need to focus on. One is L1 plants delivering to the market, the discipline on L1 plants delivering to the respective markets.

items.statement: Higher repairs and maintenance costs due to breakdowns in acquired assets (Penna, Sanghi)
items.quote: there have been a few breakdowns also of the acqu ired assets of Penna's and all. So under the planning and also under out of planning, we will do it

items.statement: Clinker factor improved from 67% to 65% in Q4 FY26
items.quote: my clinker factor has improved from 67% in December quarter to now 65%

items.statement: Premium cement pricing gap: INR50-55 for super premium, INR20-25 for premium
items.quote: the gap between my base product and the premium cement product is closer to, let us say, INR50, INR55 for the super premium and INR20, INR25 for the premium one.
